stem: In acute otitis media, what has research suggested about pain relief compared with antibiotics?

options.text: Antibiotics are significantly more effective for most children
Pain relief with NSAIDs or paracetamol is often as effective or more useful
Antibiotics must always be used to prevent hearing loss
Pain relief should be avoided because it masks meningitis
Analgesia is only helpful after antibiotics have failed

explanation: Pain relief with NSAIDs or paracetamol is often as effective or more useful than antibiotics for symptom control in acute otitis media, because many cases are self-limiting.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because antibiotics are not significantly more effective for most children with acute otitis media.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because many cases are self-limiting, and analgesia often provides adequate symptom relief without routine antibiotic treatment.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because antibiotics are not required in all cases to prevent hearing loss.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because analgesia should not be withheld; it is recommended to relieve pain.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because analgesia is appropriate early treatment, not just a backup after antibiotics fail.

source.hint: Consider the shift toward symptomatic management for self-limiting infections.
